title: Market Return Around the Clock: A Puzzle
one_line: On E-mini S&P futures 2004-2018, essentially the whole average return was earned in the 'EU-open' window (23:30-03:30 ET): 7.6% a year, Sharpe 1.67, t = 6.4; the other ~20 hours averaged about zero.

findings.statement: The EU-open window (11:30 pm to 3:30 am ET) accounts for essentially all of the E-mini S&P 500's average return.
findings.evidence: 7.6% annualised, Sharpe 1.67, t = 6.4; rest of the day about -0.8% a year. Tick data 2004-2018.

findings.statement: The pattern is positive in every year, calendar month and weekday, and similar in both halves of the sample.
findings.evidence: Trade-price and mid-quote returns nearly identical; Bonferroni-type tests reported.

findings.statement: A buy-before / sell-after EU-open rule is profitable after conservative costs, and better when VIX and Asian-session volatility are rising.
findings.evidence: Timing version: Sharpe about 1.2 after costs, high out-of-sample R2; capacity about $50m a year (as reported in the Alpha Architect summary).

findings.statement: VIX futures rise during Asian hours and fall sharply around the European open.
findings.evidence: Used as evidence for uncertainty resolution.

why.pattern: Risk premium for bearing uncertainty, paid when information that built up while the US was closed is resolved by European investors.
why.mechanism: Uncertainty accumulates during Asian hours (VIX futures rise); European participants process it at their open; the uncertainty premium is realised in that window.
why.who_is_forced: Holders of equity exposure through the Asian session bear unresolved uncertainty and are paid when it resolves.
why.why_it_persists: Thin, operationally awkward window for most US investors; capacity is limited (~$50m/yr).
why.what_would_kill_it: Overnight trading becoming crowded (ETFs/24h trading), or the uncertainty pattern in VIX disappearing. See Boyarchenko et al. (2026): the 2-3am drift has averaged ~0 since 2021.
why.authors_explanation_vs_ours: Authors favour uncertainty resolution and reject inventory risk; Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan argue for dealer inventory risk from closing imbalances. Both predict the same window, different conditioning variables.

reported_results.headline: EU-open window: 7.6%/yr, Sharpe 1.67, t = 6.4; rest of day ~0.
reported_results.costs_included: Conservative estimates (not detailed in the summary read).

tradable_edge: Hold ES only in the European-open window (about 23:30-03:30 ET, or the tighter 02:00-03:00 ET), flat otherwise. Condition on rising Asian-session volatility. Must be checked post-2021, when the related 2-3am drift reportedly vanished.
angles: Long ES 23:30→03:30 ET every night vs 02:00→03:00 ET
Only when the prior US session closed down (Boyarchenko asymmetry) or Asian-session range is above its 15-day average

decay_risk.reason: Published 2020-2023; the same authors' window (2-3am) has averaged ~0 since 2021 per Boyarchenko et al. (2026).

data_fit: ES 1-min (ETH + RTH) Dec 2013 → Sep 2026 in clean_ES_master.parquet; NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026. 2024+ is protected in the backtest project. ETH bars cover the window.
caveats: Read via the Alpha Architect summary and the abstract listing, not the full PDF; numbers are as reported there.
Sample ends 2018; ES overnight volume roughly doubled in 2020.
